newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia and NATO resume talks on partnership pact.
newsitem.headline: Russia and NATO resume talks on partnership pact.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and NATO Secretary General Javier Solana resumed talks on Wednesday to try to finalise a deal for a peaceful new relationship, Interfax news agency said.

The two men returned to the foreign ministry mansion in central Moscow where they spent six hours on Tuesday discussing the document which would shape their relations and address some of Russia's concerns about NATO's planned expansion eastwards.
Solana arrived by car and entered the building without talking to reporters.
Russian and NATO officials have made no statements about how the talks are going. Interfax said a statement was expected when the negotiations ended.
President Boris Yeltsin wants to sign an agreement with NATO in Paris on May 27 and said last week the deal was "98 percent" ready.
But he has also said he will not sign an unsatisfactory agreement and he told Primakov to take a tough line in the sixth round of Russia-NATO talks on the pact.
Yeltsin said last week Russia would not back NATO's plans to invite some eastern European countries to join the alliance at a summit in Madrid in July.
But he wants a deal to ensure a peaceful partnership with the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation and keep relations with the West on track.
Russia wants a say in NATO decisions and guarantees that the alliance's military structures and nuclear weapons would never move eastwards. NATO is reluctant to give binding assurances.
